text:
Maya Li: Heads-up — ACME (acct: acme-prod) reported intermittent high TTFB on streaming responses for /v1/chat/stream. p95 TTFB jumped from ~180ms to ~800ms starting around 2024-11-02 03:00 UTC. Non-streaming (sync) total latency looks unchanged. They said most responses are very short (1-3 tokens) so chunking/coalescing might be the culprit.

Customer repro (minimal):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-1-mini" 
```
They attached a few request ids: req_8a45f1c2, req_8a45f1d9. Can eng-runtime / SRE take a look? I can share deeper logs if needed. :eyes:

Carlos Nguyen: Thanks Maya. Can you paste the full request ids + the account id (you included acme-prod — tx). Were there any infra deploys around that time? Also does this reproduce from our eu-west-1 LB or only from the customer's network?

Maya Li: Account id: acct_0042. No deploys on the customer side; they tested from multiple office locations. I checked our internal deploy log — no code deploys to runtime between 02:30-03:30 UTC. I'll run the repro from eu-west1 now and post numbers.

Priya Patel: I pulled the runtime deploy history — we did ship a change last week (commit 1773445000) that adjusts the streaming chunk coalescing heuristic. Primary change: increased coalesce window from 8ms -> 40ms to reduce tiny-chunk overhead on heavy traffic. That reduces CPU and network overhead in our benchmarks, but it will increase TTFB for very short responses or clients with low RTT variance.

Priya Patel: Hypothesis: for requests that produce 1-3 tokens, the runtime is waiting up to the coalesce window before flushing, which raises observed TTFB. Combined with occasional network stalls / packets being coalesced at TCP level, p95 spikes.

Jared Kim: SRE data shows a modest uptick in retransmits and small packet delays for the eu-west-1 host pool around the same timeframe — not a full outage but enough to make coalescing more likely to wait. I'm seeing some NIC-level queues for a subset of instances (ENA driver counters). I'll collect tcpdump snippets.

Carlos Nguyen: Can you share a quick repro curl that matches the customer's pattern (short output)? Also want to confirm: do we see the same behaviour with HTTP/2 streaming vs SSE?

Maya Li: Repro I ran from eu-west-1 bastion:
```bash
# 100 requests, measure TTFB (Event stream first chunk)
for i in {1..100}; do 
  start=$(date +%s%3N); 
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-1-mini&prompt=hi" | head -n1 >/dev/null; 
  ttfb=$(( $(date +%s%3N) - start )); 
  echo $ttfb; 
done | sort -n | awk 'NR==90{printf "p90=%s\n",$1}; NR==95{printf "p95=%s\n",$1}; NR==99{printf "p99=%s\n",$1}'
```
Results: p90 ~200ms, p95 ~820ms, p99 ~1.4s. Non-streaming POST to /v1/chat (same prompt) p95 ~210ms.

Priya Patel: Good reproductible numbers — thanks. Quick mitigations: 
- Customer-side: if possible, use sync endpoint (non-stream) for tiny responses.
- Immediate server-side knobs we can expose: STREAM_COALESCE_MS (override), or a per-request header x-redwood-stream-flush=1 to force immediate flush after each token. We can also allow a chunk_size=1 override to flush earlier.

Priya Patel: Short-term plan: roll a canary tweak to reduce coalesce window to 12ms for routes where median token count < 6. That should regain p95 TTFB for short responses while keeping benefits for larger payloads. Filed INF-4823.

Jared Kim: For investigation: capture 1 minute tcpdump and trusses/strace on affected runtime worker while reproducing. Commands:
```bash
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/ttfb-cap.pcap host <worker-ip> and port 443
# on worker: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60; perf script > /tmp/perf.svg
```
I'll correlate with NIC metrics (ENA tx_queue stats).

Carlos Nguyen: Customer asks for quick workaround they can apply now. We should offer simple headers they can pass (if we can support immediately) or a tenant-side config we can toggle. Maya — can we ask them to try adding an HTTP header to request immediate flush? If we don't have a public header yet we can flip a feature flag for their tenant.

Maya Li: I'll ask the customer to try a fallback — use the non-streaming path for the next 24h while we run a canary. I'll also ask if they can enable HTTP/2 from their client to see if it changes chunking behavior.

Priya Patel: Action items (short term):
- Enable per-tenant override: streaming.flush_immediate=true for acct_0042 (runtime flag) — I can flip this for them now.
- Canary deploy coalesce-window=12ms for 10% of traffic in eu-west-1 for the next 2 hours, monitor p95/p99 for streaming routes.
- Add telemetry: per-request coalesce-delay histogram + trace-span when flush occurs.

deploy-bot: Scheduled: canary deploy INF-4823-coalesce-tweak to eu-west-1 (10%) — start 1773456900, monitor window 2h.

Jared Kim: I'll watch NIC metrics and packet loss after the canary. If the canary improves p95 without new errors we can expand. If NIC-layer delays persist we may need to involve cloud infra.

Carlos Nguyen: For customer-facing communication:
- Tell them we've identified a coalescing heuristic change as likely cause.
- We're flipping a tenant flag to force immediate flush for them and running a canary to reduce global coalesce window.
- Ask them to try non-streaming fallback and (optionally) HTTP/2 if feasible.

Maya Li: I'll message the customer now with those steps and ask for a 1-2 hour window to validate after the tenant flag + canary. I'll post back with customer measurements. Thanks all. :pray:

Priya Patel: Follow-up note: longer-term we want an adaptive algorithm that uses observed RTT/jitter + token-size distribution to dynamically pick flush delay per connection. INF-4823 tracks that.

Maya Li (later): Customer confirmed p95 dropped to ~210ms after we flipped streaming.flush_immediate=true for them. They're okay with temporary tenant flag; asked for ETA on global fix. I'll keep thread updated.

Carlos Nguyen: Great — mark this as resolved for the customer. Keep INF-4823 open for the global fix and add ACME as impacted customer in the ticket.

Jared Kim: Closing loop on SRE side — nothing else indicating a broader network outage. We'll continue monitoring.

Priya Patel: I'll proceed with the canary expansion plan if metrics stay green. Thanks team.
